feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, though it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently present a coherent senior profile in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications.  
- Strong credibility signals: long tenure and progression at one organization, relevant scale metrics, and concrete platforms/tools strengthen trust.  
- Good writing quality overall: no major misspellings or obvious grammar errors; tone is professional and terminology is current and appropriate.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “advised,” “developed”) without showing results such as growth, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: header uses “DAVIS” in all caps while the rest does not; punctuation/list style varies (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; some sections use sentence-style bullets while others use fragments).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a tighter emphasis on current, high-value strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more active, executive language like “leading modernization of” or “scaling.”
- Add 1–2 concrete scope signals from recent roles (e.g., enterprise web estates, analytics ecosystems, multi-publisher environments) to increase specificity.
- Trim the list of functions so the intro highlights the most relevant leadership areas: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects and skills; “AI-enabled content experiences” is more specific.
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered in experience and skills, so it may not need prominence in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased as broader capability areas rather than repeating near-identical wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Replace vague or overlapping items with more distinctive strengths: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream, and studio operations
- Consider reducing to 6–7 items to increase scanability and emphasize the most senior, recent strengths.
- Standardize style by spelling out “and” instead of mixing “&” with other constructions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently with action + platform + result.
- Tighten wording: e.g., “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace vague phrases like “continued campaign growth” with more concrete value, such as scalability, reuse, or audience engagement.
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work closely overlap with recent NACo roles; keep this section project-focused and avoid repeating responsibilities.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “production and distribution” are broad and may duplicate strengths already shown in the header and skills sections.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Make it feel clearly consultant-level by emphasizing scoped advisory work, technical delivery, and any early outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and cross-channel governance for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“build and refine,” “deliver,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed workflows…,” “Implemented Drupal microsite templates…,” “Led AI search pilot…”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/templates launched, teams supported, publishers trained, search/content efficiency gains, engagement or production improvements.
- Tighten to 4–5 bullets max, e.g. combine governance + workflows + analytics into one bullet and separate the AI-enabled search initiative as a standout item.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording repeats themes already covered in “Director of Digital Media” (governance, analytics, enterprise web improvement, Drupal).
- Avoid reusing “organization-wide communications” and broad channel lists unless this role adds distinct consulting outcomes.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale indicators, but it’s too long and overlaps with the adjacent NACo roles. Focus this item on director-level transformation, team leadership, and enterprise outcomes rather than repeating channel management details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading team operations, platform strategy, analytics, governance, and budget across web, email, social, and video.”
- Consolidate channel oversight into one line and prioritize the biggest wins: website migration, analytics modernization, and in-house studio build.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, production cost savings, engagement growth, or stakeholder adoption.
- Example structure:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia content.
- Modernized analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role.
- Governance/workflow language also appears in the current consultant role; keep this version focused on enterprise transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at the associate-director level.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial operations.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy and member communications.”
- Make workflow bullets more active and specific: “Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and cross-department alignment.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/standards bullet; keep this version focused on coordination and execution, not governance.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling and formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current strengths: strategy, governance, and audience-centered execution.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy and transformation
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “communications” or “content operations” instead of “messaging”/“planning” for a more senior, enterprise tone.
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience: governance, transformation, cross-channel leadership, and audience strategy are best supported by 2022–present roles.
- If space allows, consider one more distinctive phrase such as “platform modernization” to reflect the Drupal migration and systems work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” in Core Competencies; choose one framing consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Make it more strategic and recent by grouping skills around platform modernization and execution rather than listing every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Lead with higher-value, recent strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation.
- Tighten phrasing: change “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clearer business value.
- If possible, align wording with recent impact from experience, e.g., “enterprise Drupal platforms” or “large-scale CMS migrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave tool-by-tool detail to that section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns well with the recent Director/Consultant roles, but it reads as a raw tool list. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic so it reinforces seniority rather than repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as grouped capabilities, not just platforms: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery” → “Analytics stack: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Tighten and elevate the business value: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and leadership reporting”
- Make “KPI design” more specific: “KPI framework design” or “KPI development and performance measurement”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics stack: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- Tool names also appear in the 2022–2024 role, so this section should emphasize capability and outcomes, not just platforms.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles. Make it more senior, systems-oriented, and tied to the in-house studio/event capability you built.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic tasks with higher-value phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio system operation,” “Virtual event production workflows.”
- Emphasize leadership/ownership over execution where accurate: e.g., “Studio buildout and operations” instead of just “Studio operations.”
- Tighten to 4 bullets max and keep parallel structure; suggested version:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- PTZ camera and in-house studio system operation
- Multimedia production workflows and run-of-show coordination

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; consider simplifying one.
- Avoid overstating older hands-on production if current positioning is more strategic leadership.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and currently duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most recent, highest-impact platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If formatting allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise CMS, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep it concise; avoid turning this into another skills paragraph since impact already appears in recent NACo roles.
- If space is tight, consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for implementation skills only.
- Drupal and CMS modernization are already strongly evidenced in recent work experience, so don’t repeat descriptive claims here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current, implementation-focused, and selective.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning and older terms unless actively used recently: change “HTML5 • CSS3” to “HTML/CSS”; keep jQuery only if it reflects current hands-on work.
- Add brief scope/impact if format allows: “Front-end implementation, tagging, lightweight serverless tools, and deployment automation.”
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “JavaScript and jQuery” plus “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact same phrasing in both sections.
- If GTM is central to analytics rather than implementation, consider moving it to Analytics/Optimization instead.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from app list to capability-led wording, e.g. “Workflow automation & collaboration systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project and team coordination tools: Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello, Slack, Teams.”
- Put the most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier should lead because they best support your recent systems/automation narrative.
- Cut one or two lower-value collaboration tools if space is tight; too many PM/chat platforms dilute the stronger automation signal.
- If accurate, add a light outcome cue in adjacent experience instead of here, such as “built cross-team workflow systems” or “streamlined publishing coordination,” since this section itself should stay concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello/Slack/Teams are generic unless tied to process improvement elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform breadth and engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show level of use, e.g. **administration, campaign deployment, segmentation, and newsletter operations**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency/strength

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding broad claims like “email newsletters” or “audience engagement” here; those are already covered in Work Experience
- Don’t repeat analytics or workflow language already captured under Analytics and Automation & Workflow Systems

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and doesn’t yet signal level of use or business value. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack line and avoid generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B test design • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI/dashboard reporting** to sound more outcome-oriented and less vague.
- Replace **A/B testing** with **A/B test design** only if you actively planned/ran experiments; otherwise remove it.
- Order tools by strongest/recentest usage, with GA4/BigQuery/Power BI first to align with your 2022–present analytics infrastructure work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other.
- If space is tight, drop either **Looker Studio** or **Power BI** only if one was clearly secondary.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer action/result language: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored a junior digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; here, frame it as launching or early producing rather than expanding.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is similar to later governance/operations bullets; keep this version lighter and more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination scope and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Cut vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific verb such as “produced” or “developed” if accurate.
- If possible, add scale or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, stakeholders served, or types of materials produced.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2018 and 2018–2024 roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Since later entries already establish video/digital leadership, use this item to show origins in research/program support plus podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item currently reads broad and slightly dated relative to your more senior recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize production capability without repeating the stronger “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” skills section.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
- Replace with a tighter list: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing/production • Livestream production support**
- Use parallel phrasing: keep this item tool-focused, and move workflow language like “studio operations” or “livestream workflows” to the existing multimedia/topline skills section.
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier instead of extra nouns, e.g. **broadcast-quality video editing** or **multicam livestream support**.
